"""Remove the white air-hockey mallet from the complete source timeline.

The shot is from a locked camera.  The white mallet is the only object that
travels through the lower-left half of the playing surface, so its path is
isolated there by temporal foreground segmentation.  Pixels are reconstructed
from clean observations of the same static table coordinate in other source
frames.  This preserves the source render's grain, table gradient, and the
unaffected red/blue mallets exactly.
"""
from pathlib import Path
import numpy as np
import cv2
import artifact_io

CASE_DIR = Path(__file__).resolve().parent


def make_video():
    src = np.load(CASE_DIR / "source_pixels.npz")["rgb"]
    assert src.shape == (96, 144, 256, 3) and src.dtype == np.uint8
    n, h, w, _ = src.shape
    yy, xx = np.mgrid[:h, :w]

    # Static-camera temporal background.  At every pixel the mallet is absent
    # for most of the shot; using a central temporal estimate therefore reveals
    # the original purple playing surface (including its lighting gradient).
    bg = np.median(src, axis=0).astype(np.uint8)
    diff = np.max(np.abs(src.astype(np.int16) - bg[None].astype(np.int16)), axis=3)

    # Only this polygon can be traversed by the white mallet.  Excluding the
    # center/right protects all markings plus the red and blue mallets.
    path_roi = np.zeros((h, w), np.uint8)
    cv2.fillPoly(path_roi, [np.array([
        [45, 72], [111, 62], [116, 81], [104, 91],
        [148, 105], [148, 119], [73, 104], [45, 92]
    ], np.int32)], 1)

    frames = src.copy()
    kernel3 = np.ones((3, 3), np.uint8)
    kernel5 = np.ones((5, 5), np.uint8)
    masks = []
    for t in range(n):
        im = src[t]
        # White neutral plastic and its bright, low-saturation rim.
        mx = im.max(axis=2).astype(np.int16)
        mn = im.min(axis=2).astype(np.int16)
        neutral_bright = (mn > 167) & ((mx - mn) < 57)

        # The rendered mallet also carries a soft gray cast shadow.  Start from
        # temporal-change pixels near white plastic and grow over the complete
        # compact moving object rather than globally thresholding the surface.
        seeds = (neutral_bright & (diff[t] > 12) & (path_roi > 0)).astype(np.uint8)
        seeds = cv2.morphologyEx(seeds, cv2.MORPH_CLOSE, kernel3)
        ncc, lab, stats, _ = cv2.connectedComponentsWithStats(seeds, 8)
        core = np.zeros((h, w), np.uint8)
        for j in range(1, ncc):
            x, y, ww, hh, area = stats[j]
            # Actual white-mallet components have appreciable compact area.
            if area >= 5 and ww <= 24 and hh <= 20:
                core[lab == j] = 1

        # Expand over the base and shadow, constrained to temporally variant
        # pixels and a modest halo.  Opening removes isolated compression grain.
        halo = cv2.dilate(core, kernel5, iterations=2)
        moving = ((diff[t] > 7) & (halo > 0) & (path_roi > 0)).astype(np.uint8)
        mask = cv2.dilate((core | moving), kernel3, iterations=2)
        mask &= path_roi
        masks.append(mask)

        # Use per-pixel clean source samples where possible.  Median is robust
        # here because the white mallet occupies every coordinate briefly.
        # A feathered boundary avoids a synthetic edge in the source grain.
        alpha = cv2.GaussianBlur(mask.astype(np.float32), (0, 0), 0.75)
        alpha = np.clip(alpha, 0, 1)[..., None]
        frames[t] = np.clip(im * (1.0 - alpha) + bg * alpha + 0.5, 0, 255).astype(np.uint8)

    return frames, np.stack(masks)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    frames, masks = make_video()
    changed = np.any(frames != np.load(CASE_DIR / "source_pixels.npz")["rgb"], axis=3)
    print("edited pixels/frame: min=%d median=%d max=%d" % (
        changed.sum((1, 2)).min(), np.median(changed.sum((1, 2))), changed.sum((1, 2)).max()))
    artifact_io.save(frames, CASE_DIR)

    spec = json.loads(path.read_text()) if path.is_file() else {}
    n, h, w, fps = (spec.get("frames", 20), spec.get("height", 144), spec.get("width", 256), spec.get("fps", 4))
    assert frames.shape == (n, h, w, 3) and frames.dtype == np.uint8, frames.shape
    audio_spec = spec.get("audio")
    audio_url = None
    if audio_spec:
        samples = round(n / fps * audio_spec["sample_rate"])
        pcm = np.asarray(audio)
        if pcm.ndim == 1:
            pcm = pcm[:, None]
        assert pcm.shape == (samples, audio_spec["channels"]) and pcm.dtype == np.int16, (pcm.shape, pcm.dtype)
        with wave.open(str(case_dir / "audio.wav"), "wb") as handle:
            handle.setnchannels(audio_spec["channels"])
            handle.setsampwidth(2)
            handle.setframerate(audio_spec["sample_rate"])
            handle.writeframes(pcm.astype("<i2").tobytes())
        audio_url = "data:audio/wav;base64," + base64.b64encode((case_dir / "audio.wav").read_bytes()).decode()
    values = frames.astype(np.uint32)
    packed = (values[:, :, :, 0] << 16) | (values[:, :, :, 1] << 8) | values[:, :, :, 2]
    tensor = packed.transpose(1, 2, 0)
    np.savez_compressed(case_dir / "pixels.npz", pixels=tensor)

    folder = case_dir / "frames"
    folder.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
    for index, frame in enumerate(frames):
        Image.fromarray(frame).save(folder / f"{index:02d}.png")

    sheet = Image.new("RGB", (w * 4, (h + 21) * 2), (25, 28, 35))
    draw = ImageDraw.Draw(sheet)
    for index, frame_index in enumerate(np.linspace(0, n - 1, 8).round().astype(int)):
        x, y = (index % 4) * w, (index // 4) * (h + 21)
        draw.text((x + 5, y + 3), f"frame {frame_index:02d} · {frame_index / fps:.2f}s", fill="white")
        sheet.paste(Image.fromarray(frames[frame_index]), (x, y + 21))
    sheet.save(case_dir / "inspection.png")

    transition = Image.new("RGB", (w * 4, h * 2 + 21), (25, 28, 35))
    draw = ImageDraw.Draw(transition)
    for index, frame_index in enumerate(min(i, n-1) for i in range(4)):
        x = index * w
        draw.text((x + 5, 4), f"frame {frame_index:02d} · {frame_index / fps:.2f}s", fill="white")
        transition.paste(Image.fromarray(frames[frame_index]), (x, 21))
        transition.paste(Image.fromarray(frames[frame_index]).resize((w, h), Image.Resampling.NEAREST), (x, h + 21))
    transition.save(case_dir / "transition_check.png")

    encode = lambda array: base64.b64encode(np.asarray(array, dtype="<u4").tobytes()).decode()
    deltas = []
    for index in range(1, n):
        current = packed[index].reshape(-1)
        previous = packed[index - 1].reshape(-1)
        positions = np.flatnonzero(current != previous)
        packet = []
        if len(positions):
            bounds = np.r_[0, np.flatnonzero(np.diff(positions) > 1) + 1, len(positions)]
            for start, end in zip(bounds[:-1], bounds[1:]):
                offset = int(positions[start])
                count = int(end - start)
                packet.extend([offset, count])
                packet.extend(current[offset:offset + count].tolist())
        deltas.append(encode(packet))
    data = {
        "id": case_dir.name,
        "width": w, "height": h, "frames": n, "fps": fps, "audio": audio_url,
        "first": encode(packed[0].reshape(-1)),
        "deltas": deltas,
        "caption": (case_dir / "prompt.txt").read_text().strip(),
    }
    template = (Path(__file__).parent / "player_template.html").read_text()
    payload = json.dumps(data, separators=(",", ":"), ensure_ascii=False).replace("<", "\\u003c")
    (case_dir / "index.html").write_text(template.replace("__ID__", case_dir.name).replace("__DATA__", payload))

\"\"\"Remove the white air-hockey mallet from the complete source timeline.

The shot is from a locked camera.  The white mallet is the only object that
travels through the lower-left half of the playing surface, so its path is
isolated there by temporal foreground segmentation.  Pixels are reconstructed
from clean observations of the same static table coordinate in other source
frames.  This preserves the source render's grain, table gradient, and the
unaffected red/blue mallets exactly.
\"\"\"
from pathlib import Path
import numpy as np
import cv2
import artifact_io

CASE_DIR = Path(__file__).resolve().parent


def make_video():
    src = np.load(CASE_DIR / \"source_pixels.npz\")[\"rgb\"]
    assert src.shape == (96, 144, 256, 3) and src.dtype == np.uint8
    n, h, w, _ = src.shape
    yy, xx = np.mgrid[:h, :w]

    # Static-camera temporal background.  At every pixel the mallet is absent
    # for most of the shot; using a central temporal estimate therefore reveals
    # the original purple playing surface (including its lighting gradient).
    bg = np.median(src, axis=0).astype(np.uint8)
    diff = np.max(np.abs(src.astype(np.int16) - bg[None].astype(np.int16)), axis=3)

    # Only this polygon can be traversed by the white mallet.  Excluding the
    # center/right protects all markings plus the red and blue mallets.
    path_roi = np.zeros((h, w), np.uint8)
    cv2.fillPoly(path_roi, [np.array([
        [45, 72], [111, 62], [116, 81], [104, 91],
        [148, 105], [148, 119], [73, 104], [45, 92]
    ], np.int32)], 1)

    frames = src.copy()
    kernel3 = np.ones((3, 3), np.uint8)
    kernel5 = np.ones((5, 5), np.uint8)
    masks = []
    for t in range(n):
        im = src[t]
        # White neutral plastic and its bright, low-saturation rim.
        mx = im.max(axis=2).astype(np.int16)
        mn = im.min(axis=2).astype(np.int16)
        neutral_bright = (mn > 167) & ((mx - mn) < 57)

        # The rendered mallet also carries a soft gray cast shadow.  Start from
        # temporal-change pixels near white plastic and grow over the complete
        # compact moving object rather than globally thresholding the surface.
        seeds = (neutral_bright & (diff[t] > 12) & (path_roi > 0)).astype(np.uint8)
        seeds = cv2.morphologyEx(seeds, cv2.MORPH_CLOSE, kernel3)
        ncc, lab, stats, _ = cv2.connectedComponentsWithStats(seeds, 8)
        core = np.zeros((h, w), np.uint8)
        for j in range(1, ncc):
            x, y, ww, hh, area = stats[j]
            # Actual white-mallet components have appreciable compact area.
            if area >= 5 and ww <= 24 and hh <= 20:
                core[lab == j] = 1

        # Expand over the base and shadow, constrained to temporally variant
        # pixels and a modest halo.  Opening removes isolated compression grain.
        halo = cv2.dilate(core, kernel5, iterations=2)
        moving = ((diff[t] > 7) & (halo > 0) & (path_roi > 0)).astype(np.uint8)
        mask = cv2.dilate((core | moving), kernel3, iterations=2)
        mask &= path_roi
        masks.append(mask)

        # Use per-pixel clean source samples where possible.  Median is robust
        # here because the white mallet occupies every coordinate briefly.
        # A feathered boundary avoids a synthetic edge in the source grain.
        alpha = cv2.GaussianBlur(mask.astype(np.float32), (0, 0), 0.75)
        alpha = np.clip(alpha, 0, 1)[..., None]
        frames[t] = np.clip(im * (1.0 - alpha) + bg * alpha + 0.5, 0, 255).astype(np.uint8)

    return frames, np.stack(masks)


if __name__ == \"__main__\":
    frames, masks = make_video()
    changed = np.any(frames "'!= np.load(CASE_DIR / "source_pixels.npz")["rgb"], axis=3)
    print("edited pixels/frame: min=%d median=%d max=%d" % (
        changed.sum((1, 2)).min(), np.median(changed.sum((1, 2))), changed.sum((1, 2)).max()))
    artifact_io.save(frames, CASE_DIR)
